definition: An informal term for a group of infrastructure products from HashiCorp used together to provision, secure, network, or run services.
example: An infrastructure team combines infrastructure provisioning and secrets management tools in a deployment workflow.
sense_note: The exact products included vary with the organization.

definition: A preventive food safety method that identifies hazards and specifies control points, limits, monitoring, and corrective actions.
example: A food producer monitors a documented critical control point and records corrective actions when limits are exceeded.

definition: Preventing the spread of hazardous substances and coordinating their control through authorized response procedures.
example: A trained response team isolates an affected area and coordinates specialist cleanup.

definition: Moving, storing, and using hazardous substances in accordance with their classifications and applicable safety procedures.
example: A facility checks storage compatibility and labeling before accepting a chemical shipment.

definition: U.S. healthcare program regulations historically associated with the Health Care Financing Administration.
example: A policy reviewer consults a historical rule to interpret an older Medicare contract.
sense_note: HCFA was renamed CMS; identify the particular regulation, program, and date.

definition: A wearable screen or optical device that presents images in front of a user's eyes.
example: A training system displays a virtual environment through a headset worn by a participant.

definition: Supporting people in setting and following their own goals for health-related habits and well-being.
example: A coach helps a client set a manageable walking goal and review their progress.

definition: A standardized set of performance measures used to assess healthcare quality and health plan performance.
example: A health plan reports an eligible preventive screening measure using HEDIS specifications.

definition: Planning the location, capacity, layout, and services of healthcare facilities to meet operational and patient needs.
example: A planning team estimates how many examination rooms a new clinic requires.

definition: Setting priorities, objectives, and resource plans for a healthcare organization or initiative.
example: A hospital compares service demand and capacity before deciding where to expand.

definition: Software used to configure, adjust, or assess the operation of hearing aids.
example: An audiologist uses fitting software to tailor amplification to the wearer's hearing assessment.

definition: Shaping a piece of wood by applying heat and bending it to a form.
example: A furniture maker produces a curved wooden component for a chair.

definition: A visualization method that maps values to colors over a matrix, surface, or set of locations.
example: An analyst colors each matrix cell based on a measured error rate.

definition: Operating large powered machinery safely and effectively for work such as construction, extraction, or material movement.
example: A trained operator uses an excavator to move material within an approved work zone.

definition: Driving or maneuvering vehicles with substantial size or weight while accounting for load, clearance, and stopping distance.
example: A licensed commercial driver plans a route with adequate clearance for a loaded truck.

definition: An open-source web crawler designed to collect web content for preservation and archival use.
example: An archive uses Heritrix to preserve a public website within an approved collection scope.

definition: A named restriction enzyme that recognizes particular DNA sequences and cuts double-stranded DNA.
sense_note: Non-operational description; distinguish from other restriction enzymes without supplying recognition or cleavage details.

definition: A monitored decoy resource used to detect or study potentially unauthorized activity in a controlled setting.
example: A security team records unexpected interactions with an authorized decoy system.

definition: A social media management platform for publishing, monitoring, and reporting across accounts.
example: A communications team schedules approved posts for several channels from one interface.

definition: A system historically used by the U.S. Department of Defense to manage and monitor security controls on host computers.
sense_note: Confirm the program generation and distinguish it from successor endpoint security systems.

definition: Managing hospitality operations across lodging and food service, including staffing, service quality, and financial performance.
example: A manager coordinates hotel occupancy plans with restaurant staffing for a convention.

definition: Managing lodging operations such as reservations, reception, housekeeping, staffing, and guest service.
example: A hotel manager adjusts staffing to meet expected occupancy.

definition: A historical web browser from Sun Microsystems written in Java.
example: A computing historian examines how HotJava presented web pages in its period.

definition: A family of Hewlett-Packard minicomputers used for computing and industrial or instrumentation applications.
example: A computing museum demonstrates an archived program on an HP 2100 system.

definition: A Hewlett-Packard desktop computer model designed for technical computing and color graphics.
example: A computing museum demonstrates technical plots on a preserved HP 9845C.

definition: An application lifecycle management product for connecting requirements, testing, defects, and release quality records.
example: A quality team links a software defect and its regression test to the underlying requirement.
sense_note: Historical HP branding; confirm current product ownership and edition when relevant.

definition: A historical family of Hewlett-Packard desktop computers marketed for small businesses.
example: An IT archivist identifies a recovered HP Brio as a business desktop.

definition: A historical Hewlett-Packard product family of handheld and pocket computers.
example: A collector demonstrates the organizer applications on an HP Jornada handheld.

definition: A historical Hewlett-Packard graphical software environment built for personal computers running Windows.
example: A computing historian examines NewWave's object-oriented desktop concepts.

definition: A software test management product used to organize requirements, test runs, and defects.
example: A test lead records regression results and links failed cases to defects.
sense_note: Confirm the applicable Quality Center or ALM edition and historical branding.

definition: A Hewlett-Packard management application for discovering, monitoring, and administering supported server infrastructure.
example: An operator reviews alerts and inventory for supported servers in a managed environment.

definition: A historical automated functional testing tool that recorded and replayed interactions with graphical applications.
example: A QA team used WinRunner to regression-test a data-entry screen.

definition: Using workforce data to assess patterns, evaluate human resources programs, and support personnel decisions.
example: An analyst examines retention rates across cohorts to assess an onboarding program.

definition: Creating email content using HTML and email-compatible layout, styling, and accessibility practices.
example: A communications team builds an invitation and checks that it renders in several email clients.

definition: Applying appropriate HTML elements and markup to structure content for web presentation and interpretation.
example: An author uses semantic headings and lists to organize a help page.

definition: A JavaScript compatibility library that enabled early versions of Internet Explorer to recognize and style HTML5 elements.
example: A historical website includes html5shiv so old browsers can display the new section elements.

definition: A customer relationship management platform for organizing contacts, companies, deals, and interactions.
example: A sales team tracks opportunities and follow-up tasks in a shared CRM.

definition: Connecting human capital management systems with related applications or data flows.
example: An integration specialist synchronizes employee record changes between HR and payroll systems.

definition: Designing systems around human capabilities and limitations to improve usability, safety, and performance.
example: An engineer evaluates whether operators can read and interpret emergency controls quickly and reliably.
